title: Father's early band with Richard Payne and Big Eye Louie
summary: He recalls his father's band, with Payne on guitar, Big Eye Louie on clarinet, called Imperial or Superior; his father was manager rather than leader.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you ever hear him play bass much?

Oh, yeah, Bill. Yeah. I used to follow my dad a lot. I heard that when he was ten years old, I remember, when he had the band with Bump and Peter Bocall and Violet and Richard Payne. And Walter Brunley, I think the drum player was named. Buddy Johnson's trombone.
And the ghetto player was Richard. Richard, I forget his last name, but anyhow.
Is that Payne? Richard Payne. Richard Payne. That's right. Richard Payne. That's right. Yeah. Who was the clarinet, do you remember?
Yeah, Big Eye Louie. Big Eye Louie. Yeah, Louie Nelson.
What was the name of that band?
Is it Imperial? You sure? Yeah. Or was it Superior, maybe? Yeah, yeah.
I think it was Imperial or Superior, one of those bands. I just remember quite the name, but Imperial or Superior, one of those names.
And your father, I guess, was manager, said that on his cap and that picture.
Well, he was manager of the band, yeah, but we didn't have such thing as leader then, it was manager then. Yeah.
Where did you live in those days? In the same neighborhood, or had you moved?
Well, no, Bill. I lived in around 1200 block, two row, that's between Murray and Oich Court.
